title: Batch+Cache Troubleshooter Vignette: single-pane diagnostics & guided fixes
creator: Ava Moreno
description:
Purpose: Ship a compact, single-screen "troubleshooter" vignette inside the Redwood Console to help operators diagnose suboptimal token economics or latency regressions tied to batching and KV/prefix caching. The vignette is intentionally focused — no full policy editor — it's for fast remediation and safe rollouts. Goals:
1) Surface the most relevant signals (tokens/sec, p50/p95 latency, cache hit rate, prefix reuse) correlated to recent config changes or model rollouts.
2) Provide 3 concise, ranked remediation suggestions with estimated delta (cost %, latency ms) and confidence band.
3) Let the operator preview impact with a lightweight scenario simulator and then apply a guarded change (canary or staged rollout) with automatic fallback.
Design constraints and trade-offs: keep UI to one horizontal workspace for fast scanning. Avoid adding another modal; use collapsible panes. Show compact microcopy explaining each suggested action (why it helps, potential risk to quality). Trade-off: showing estimated savings requires a backend estimator (ENG dependency) so we provide conservative defaults and clear confidence labels.
Proposed screens/components: Overview header (service & model selector, timeframe), Signal strip (small sparklines for token rate, latency, cache hit), Root cause hints (heuristic rules e.g. "low prefix reuse on short prompts"), Ranked suggestions (Increase batch cap, Enable KV prefix caching, Relax strict latency target + apply burst mode) with estimated delta badges and a confidence meter, Simulator (input: traffic shape presets; output: projected cost & p95 change), Apply controls (radio: canary 10% -> 50% -> 100%, quick rollback button), Audit summary (change summary, link to rollout and runbook), Lightweight eval runner link (runs existing prompt set against old vs new config).
Acceptance criteria: 1) Prototype in Figma with all interactions and copy; 2) Frontend implementation handed to ENG with accessible components and unit tests; 3) Backend estimator hooks documented and mocked so QA can validate; 4) PM sign-off on microcopy and allowed default thresholds.
Accessibility notes: color contrast for confidence badges, keyboard-first interactions for simulator presets, ensure screen-reader-friendly labels for each suggestion.
Out-of-scope: full policy composer, long-term recommendation learning. This vignette is a targeted troubleshooting surface to reduce mean time to remediation for token/latency anomalies.
comments: 2026-03-01 - Ava Moreno: Initial brief and wireframe sketched during design sprint. Captured three working hypotheses for root-cause heuristics and a rough priority order for suggestions.

2026-03-03 - Product review (Lena Park): Liked single-pane approach. Request: add an 'explainability' tooltip that shows which signal triggered each suggestion (e.g., 'cache hit rate < 8% for last 30m').

2026-03-04 - Eng sync (Marco Silva): Confirmed estimator API will be available as 'estimator/v1/simulate' but with 50ms avg latency; suggested we show cached last-known estimates while waiting for real response.
2026-03-05 - Design iteration (Ethan Klein): Updated microcopy for risk/benefit badges; reduced lines of copy per suggestion to 1 sentence + 1-line why. Attached Figma prototype link.

2026-03-07 - FE review (Priya Joshi): Asked for component tokens and whether existing Badge/Tooltip components can be reused. Action: create token mapping doc and mark components for accessibility tweaks.

2026-03-08 - PM sign-off (Liam O'Connell): Approved acceptance criteria pending one UX tweak: expose 'simulate with recent traces' checkbox. Also requested a short user-help snippet for the rollout canary defaults.
2026-03-09 - QA note (Nadia Chen): Will validate simulator results against historical dashboard values; asked for a mocked API fixture for deterministic tests.
2026-03-10 - Design owner (Ava Moreno): Pushed updated frames to Figma and opened GitHub PR with prototype assets and copy doc. Marking ticket 'In Review'.
